name: Rónán Achike-Szymańska
description: Rónán Achike-Szymańska is the most famous living survivor of the Bloodwork Circuit, an Irish-Polish the Gray Zone fighter who competed in forty-one unsanctioned underground bouts between 2197 and 2203 using a patchwork of gray-market chrome — a reinforced left forearm, a pirated pain-suppression BCI, and a black-market adrenal modulator stitched into his thoracic cavity by a Tier 1 back-alley surgeon. He walked out of his final bout with a shattered orbital plate and a severed nerve cluster in his right hand, announced his retirement on a pirate feed with seventeen million simultaneous listeners, and has since become an involuntary icon of the Gray Zone survival culture. He has refused every corporate rehabilitation offer.
story_hooks: A Tier 2 documentary crew tracking Achike-Szymańska discovers he has been quietly coaching a new generation of the Gray Zone fighters — not for the Bloodwork Circuit but for something organized and purposeful that he refuses to name.

The gray-market surgeon who installed his thoracic adrenal modulator is found dead; the modulator's manufacturer — a ghost corponation — appears to have left something else inside Rónán that he doesn't know about.

A Spire legal team surfaces with documentation suggesting one of his fatal bouts was arranged by a Tier 4 gambling syndicate that also bribed the opposing fighter to lose — meaning Rónán may have killed a man who was throwing the fight.
